newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria introduces more reforms at its ports.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria introduces more reforms at its ports.

text.p: Nigeria's military government has introduced more radical reforms at the country's ports which are aimed at restoring order there.

Finance minister Anthony Ani said on Monday at a breakdown of the 1997 fiscal budget that in addition to reforms in place since 1996, a decree on ports related offences had been signed. Magistrate courts have been set up in all the ports to try offenders.
Ani did not say what penalties awaited offenders when tried and found guilty by the ports' courts.
"A task force for the clearance of undesirable elements at the ports has also been set up...and identity cards will be worn by every person entering the ports in Nigeria," Ani said.
Last year, the government tightened collection of customs dues at the ports after the Federal Finance Ministry said the customs service was lax and corrupt.
It also eliminated the chaotic procedures and delays associated with clearance of goods at the ports.
Ani said the reforms introduced in 1996 shot earnings at Nigerian ports to 55 billion naira from 39 billion naira the previous year, adding that he expected the earnings to improve in 1997.
"Scanning equipment has been purchased for easy identification of imports and to eliminate unnecessary interference in the inspection and verification of imports."
Ani said service charges for containers and palettes imposed on importers had been suspended.
